original_question: A group G is said to be invariably generated by a and b if G is generated by the conjugates ag, bh for every g, h. Let p ̸= q be fixed primes. Does every finite group embed into a finite group invariably generated by an element of order p and an element of order q?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation: it has the same hypothesis that p and q are fixed distinct primes, the same two-element invariable-generation condition, and the same universal embedding question for arbitrary finite groups.
missing_details: Use different symbols for the arbitrary finite group and the ambient overgroup; otherwise the letter G is doing two jobs at once.
Make explicit that "embed" means "isomorphic to a subgroup of".
Replace the ambiguous notation "ag, bh" by standard conjugation notation: if H is the ambient group, then a^g = g^{-1}ag and b^h = h^{-1}bh, and the condition is H = <a^g, b^h> for every g, h in H.
State explicitly that the elements a and b belong to the ambient finite group and have orders exactly p and q, respectively.
Spell out the quantifiers cleanly: p and q are fixed in advance, and for every finite group K there exists a finite group H with the required property.
refined_question: Fix distinct primes p and q. Is it true that for every finite group K there exists a finite group H containing a subgroup isomorphic to K and elements a, b in H with |a| = p and |b| = q such that, for every g, h in H, one has H = <a^g, b^h>?
justification: The nearest official formulation is the paper's Problem 21.142, which states essentially this question and nothing broader. The notebook entry itself already contains the operative definition and the exact embedding question, so the only faithful refinements are to make the subgroup-embedding meaning, conjugation notation, element orders, and quantifiers fully explicit, without broadening the scope.
